Disease burden across every breed and every age

One row per breed, one column per four months of life. Cell darkness is how many conditions are inside their onset window at that age — the whole set on one screen. The vertical rule on each row is that breed’s mean lifespan.

Read the bars as onset, not risk. A bar marks the interval in which clinical signs typically first appear in an affected dog of that breed. It says nothing about how likely this dog is to be affected, and a condition absent from a breed’s list is not excluded in that breed.

Mean lifespan is anchored to published life tables, principally McMillan et al. 2024 (Scientific Reports, 584,734 dogs) reconciled with Kennel Club survey data. Modal lifespan is estimated, not published — age-at-death distributions are left-skewed, so the most common age at death sits above the mean. It is labelled est. everywhere it appears and should be quoted as an estimate.

Onset windows are clinical consensus ranges drawn from Gough, Thomas & O’Neill, Breed Predispositions to Disease in Dogs and Cats (3rd ed.), the OFA/CHIC screening schedules, OMIA, the ACVO Blue Book, and breed-specific primary literature. Full source list and derivation notes in SOURCES.md. Version v0.5.0.
